Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at high learning rates.
Wider layers amplify update magnitudes, which makes high learning rates more unstable.
Small networks are capacity-limited, so adding width helps more than when already wide.

Deeper networks are harder to optimize at high learning rates and more prone to divergence.
